messages.author: ea0f6cc4a9d96e3b
messages.subject: Subjunc versions
parts:
Hello,
 Below are RNASeq results using two different versions of Subread and Subjunc and the default parameters:  I am interested in understanding the drop in %mapping and %junctions in the latest version.   Thanks,  Beth

V1.3.6-p1:

96% mapped

173,355 junctions


V1.4.1:  

71.9% mapped

26157 fusions

84496 indels

89593 alljunctions

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Subjunc versions
parts:
Dear Beth,

Could you please post the commands you used in this comparison?

Thanks,
Wei

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Subjunc versions
parts:
Hi Beth,

Sorry this was caused by a bug that was introduced when we added the --allJunctions argument to subjunc. This has been fixed in the latest version 1.4.2. Please download the latest version and rerun it on your data. You should get similar number of junctions.

Thanks for reporting it.

Wei

messages.author: ea0f6cc4a9d96e3b

parts:
Hi,
With version 1.4.2 I still see a decrease in the % mapping: from 96% with version V1.3.6-p1 down to 86.1% using version 1.4.2.
Thanks,
Beth

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Subjunc versions
parts:
Hi Beth,

The subjunc program in v1.3.6-p1 calls subread-align program for its initial read mapping step. The output of subread-align program contains mapping percentage information. Could you please check if the mapping percentage you mentioned (96%) was actually from the output of subread-align, but not from subjunc?

Subjunc in v1.4.* does not call subread-align program any more.

Best regards,
Wei
